column1: # obligation-kinds.tsv (harbor#1050) — every kind of unfinished work the obligations ledger tracks.
# One row per start/terminal pair. bin/status-obligations.sh folds the event bus (harbor#1043) by
# this table and by nothing else: a new producer is a row here, not new code. An event whose kind
# no row names opens nothing and closes nothing: it is refused, never guessed.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; the first non-comment row is the header)
#   kind       the obligation kind; an obligation id is <kind>:<subject>. No ':' in a kind.
#   open       ERE over the event kind that opens the row, anchored by the fold; - = no event opens it
#   close      ERE over the event kinds that close it (a terminal event repeats the open subject); - = none
#   deadline   default time allowed: <N>s|m|h|d, or - for none. An open event's data.deadline_ts wins
#   owner      who owns the row: self (<kind>:<subject>) | subject-session (session:<subject before ':'>)
#              | data-session (session:<data.session_id>, else operator) | operator
#   on_stop    abandon = a session.stop of the owner session marks the row abandoned; - = leave it
#   outlives   - or <data key>=<ERE>: a row whose open event matches survives its owner session's stop
#   reconcile  the source (or sources, comma-separated: the first to answer closes) the reconciler asks about a row that is still open
#              (bin/status-obligations.sh reconcile):
#              sessions (the registry), claude-agents, owner-session (the owner's liveness), gh-pr, gh-run,
#              sweep (the harbor-clean --record rows), deadline (nothing to read: the overdue pass is its check),
#              approval-queue (~/.local/state/harbor/approvals/queue.jsonl: an id closed there); an owner-session row that outlives its
#              session is abandoned once its deadline has passed and its dead owner wrote no transcript after it
#   opens_when - or <data key>=<ERE>: an open event opens a row only if its data key matches the ERE (anchored by the fold).
#              An event that does not is counted as matching no row: it opens nothing and is never guessed at (harbor#1049)
# Claude Code has no hook for a background tool finishing, so a background row closes only at its deadline or when its
# session ends. That is right for work whose lifetime matters (Monitor, Workflow, CronCreate, ScheduleWakeup) and noise
# for a plain background Bash, which opened a row nobody could close: `⧗N` read as a census, not as work to look at.
# The bus still records every start; only the ledger declines the Bash ones, and deleting the opens_when cell restores them.
# approval (harbor#1018, ship contract §5a.3): an approval queued for the operator, subject = the queue id; gate-approve.sh
# or gate-queue.sh close emits approval.close, and the reconciler also closes it from the queue file (approval-queue), or when the pull request
# its link names is merged or closed (gh-pr): an approval for a PR that no longer needs the operator is not owed.
# A kind with `-` for open and close is opened and closed by the reconciler alone: leftover is a sweep
# RISK/DECIDE row while the record names it, and closed by reconcile when the next record does not.
# A session has NO deadline (harbor#1115): it is not a task with a due time, it is a thing that is alive or is not. A 24h deadline
# turned every healthy session older than a day overdue, the receipt red, and findings.sh filed a finding about a working session.
# Only a session.stop, or the reconciler finding its id gone from the registry, ends it.
# Not yet a row: scheduled check (opens by CHECKS.md schedule, not by an event).
